items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names say what they do (durabilityTracker, resultLocked, failAllLocked, reportBatchDurable). Public APIs and fields have doc comments, and tricky spots are commented (e.g. 'WAL syncs are ordered...', 'prefer the durability outcome'). Short receiver names follow Go idiom.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The tracker type is clean and its functions are short. But the reporting logic is spread across db.go applyInternal, batch.go SyncWait and commit.go timing, instead of being fed from commit.go. It also detects the default handler with a fragile reflect pointer check (isNoopBatchDurable).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: All state is guarded by a mutex, and waiters use a buffered channel plus a heap with no polling. Context cancellation races are handled by checking w.index. Errors wrap sentinel values via cockroachdb/errors, limits are named constants, and the first error is latched and fans out to all waiters.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: All changes are additive (new fields, methods and hook, plus a noop default in EnsureDefaults). Non-sync commits skip all of it because everything is gated on `if sync`. Sync commits take only one tracker mutex, a small cost next to the fsync, and the existing callbacks are untouched.
